meta.title: Redaura — 伤害减少与药物检测预警基础设施
hero.sub: Redaura 允许药物检测和伤害减少组织在几秒钟内，向指定区域内的每部手机发送以其组织署名的本国语言预警。
hero.pushBody: 您附近警报：冒充 MDMA 销售的药丸含有 PMMA。发布机构：本地药检团队
stats.l1: 从审核发布到覆盖区域内手机
stats.l3: 损害减少机构的使用费用
stats.l4: 离开用户设备的位置数据
gap.p1: 凌晨1点，检测团队在音乐节现场发现了一份成分异常的样品。他们拥有检测结果、专业设备以及与现场人群建立的二十年信任。但他们唯一的预警方式是在帐篷外写白板，或向已有关注者发布动态。
gap.p2: 国家监测系统虽然拥有覆盖力，但缺乏即时响应机制。他们收集数据、分析趋势并在数周后发布指导。他们从未被设计用于在今晚将预警推送给三万部手机。
gap.heading: Redaura 连接每个人。
feat1.title: 仅限经过认证的机构发布
feat1.copy: 资质认证在创建账号前完成。现场志愿者起草警报，指定负责人确认发布。双重审核，恪守严谨。
feat2.title: 结构化警报，而非自由文本
feat2.copy: 警报由标准化字段构建。所有数值经过20多种语言的专家审核：荷兰团队发布的警告可以无缝以母语形式呈现为德语或波兰语，无翻译延迟，杜绝俚语或歧义。
feat3.title: 零追踪，保护隐私
feat3.copy: 匹配在手机本地完成——由手机自行判断是否处于预警区域。无任何数据传输，无任何日志记录，亦无法被司法调取。这是底层架构，而非设置选项。
feat4.title: 数据双向流通
feat4.copy: 由于警报是结构化的，今晚发送到手机的同一份发布内容可以以国家监测系统已能读取的格式直接送达国家监测机构。
feat.offline.title: 专为无信号区域设计。
feat.offline.body: 音乐节的移动网络往往在预警最为关键的时刻严重拥堵。应用可立即打开并显示最新缓存预警，标明上次同步时间，并在极弱信号下完成更新。预警直接随推送内容到达——即使其他内容均无法加载也可正常阅读。
app.kicker: 演示应用 — 实时原型
app.title: 一个应用。
app.note1: 用户下载一个全球统一客户端；上面的警报归属于发布它们的机构——包含其名称、Logo 和实验室编号。在地面建立的信任随预警一同传递。
app.note2: 点击警报以打开。几秒钟后推送就会送达，或在手机下方重播。
quote.text: “我们有志愿者、检测工具包和二十年建立的信任。我们比任何人都先知道哪些药丸是有危险的。我们只是无法足够快地通知大家。”
quote.attr: — 毒品检测协调员，意向试点合作伙伴
proto.lead: 预警信息以公开且文档化的格式发布——任何机构、实验室或国家级早期预警系统均可独立发布与接入。无供应商锁定，完全兼容 CAP 紧急预警国际标准。
proto.point1.title: 永久拥有
proto.point1.body: 随时导出所有预警数据、数据结构及历史记录。拒绝私有格式与封闭数据库。
proto.point2.title: 互联互通
proto.point2.body: 无缝对接现有的早期预警系统与公共安全基础设施。
proto.point3.title: 使命长存
proto.point3.body: 开放规范的生命力超越任何单一公司或机构。伤害减少公共基础设施永保开放。
proto.bridge: 创始合作伙伴将从第一天起共同参与制定技术规范 →
pilot.title: 原型已完备。协议已开源。
pilot.note:
一家在荷兰注册的非营利基金会（Stichting），在欧盟境内开发与托管。我们正在寻找三家创始合作伙伴（检测机构、同行支持网络或区域卫生部门）共同完善系统。试点伙伴将加入理事会并参与制定认证规则。

无约束力、无资金要求、无排他性。

pilot.follow: 非机构用户但也想关注进展？留下您的邮箱，我们每月推送最新动态。

Redaura — 荷兰注册的非营利基金会。
在欧盟设计、开发与托管。

__source.meta.title: Redaura — alert infrastructure for harm reduction
__source.hero.sub: Redaura lets drug-checking and harm-reduction organizations send a warning to every phone in a defined area, in seconds, in the reader's own language, credited to their organization by name.
__source.hero.pushBody: Near you: pills sold as MDMA contain PMMA. Alert by Local Drug Checking Team.
__source.stats.l1: From approval to phones in the area
__source.gap.p1: A drug-checking team finds a mislabelled sample at a festival at 1am. They have the result, the equipment, and twenty years of trust with the people at that festival. Their only way to spread the warning is a whiteboard outside the tent and a post that reaches whoever is already following them.
__source.gap.p2: National monitoring systems have the reach, but not this mandate. They aggregate, they track trends, they issue guidance over weeks. They were never built to put a warning on thirty thousand phones tonight.
__source.gap.heading: Redaura connects the two.
__source.feat1.title: Only vetted organizations publish
__source.feat1.copy: Accreditation happens before an account exists. A volunteer at the testing point drafts the alert; a designated lead releases it. Two people, every time.
__source.feat2.title: Structured alerts, not free text
__source.feat2.copy: Alerts are built from fixed fields, not written as prose. Every value is expert-reviewed in 20+ languages, so a Dutch team's warning arrives natively in Polish or German with no translation step and no room for slang or ambiguity.
__source.feat3.title: Nobody is tracked
__source.feat3.copy: Matching happens on the device — the phone works out whether it's inside an alert area. Nothing is transmitted, nothing is logged, nothing can be subpoenaed. That's the architecture, not a setting.
__source.feat4.title: The data goes both ways
__source.feat4.copy: Because alerts are structured, the same publication that reaches phones tonight can reach national monitoring tonight, in a format their systems already read.
__source.feat.offline.title: Built for dead zones.
__source.feat.offline.body: Festival cell networks saturate exactly when alerts matter most. The app opens instantly with last-known alerts, shows when it last synced, and catches up on the thinnest sliver of signal. Alerts arrive inside the push itself — readable even when nothing else loads.
__source.app.title: One app.
__source.app.note1: Users download a single global client; the alerts on it belong to the organizations that publish them — their name, their logo, their lab reference. The trust built on the ground travels with the warning.
__source.app.note2: Tap an alert to open it. A push lands a few seconds later, or replay it under the phone.
__source.quote.text: “We have the volunteers, the test kits, and twenty years of trust. We know which pills are dangerous before anyone else does. We just can't tell people fast enough.”
__source.quote.attr: — Drug checking coordinator, prospective pilot partner
__source.proto.lead: Alerts are published in an open, documented format — any org, lab, or national early-warning system can publish and consume them. Zero lock-in, fully mappable to the CAP emergency-alert standard.
__source.proto.point1.title: Yours forever
__source.proto.point1.body: Export all alert data, schemas, and history at any time. No proprietary formats or locked databases.
__source.proto.point2.title: Interoperable
__source.proto.point2.body: Connects directly to existing early-warning systems and public safety infrastructure.
__source.proto.point3.title: Mission-proof
__source.proto.point3.body: The open specification outlives any single company or organization. Harm reduction infrastructure stays public.
__source.proto.bridge: Founding partners help shape the specification from day one →
__source.pilot.title: Working prototype. Open protocol.
__source.pilot.note:
A non-profit registered in the Netherlands, built and hosted in the EU. We're looking for three founding partners — drug-checking services, peer-support networks, or regional health bodies — to shape this before it ships. Pilot partners sit on the governance board and set the accreditation rules.

Non-binding, no funding commitment, no exclusivity.
